lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Winter Around the World
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about winter weather in different countries.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about winter somewhere.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss winter weather children have experienced.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about winter weather around the world.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
resources_needed: Non-fiction text about world winter weather
key_questions: What is winter like in this country?
Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap facts found about world winter weather.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about winter somewhere in the world.

lessons.title: Comparing Temperatures Around the World
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare and order temperatures from different countries.
success_criteria: I can compare two temperatures.
I can order 3+ countries by temperature.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing winter temperatures from different countries using simple data.
lessons.independent_task: Children order country temperature cards from coldest to warmest.
key_questions: Which country is coldest in winter?
Can you order these three?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note temperature comparison consolidation applied to world geography — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Compare winter temperatures of places you know.

lessons.title: Where Does It Snow?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify regions where snow is common in winter.
success_criteria: I can name a snowy region.
I can say why it snows there.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss whether it snows where children live.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss regions where snow is common (northern Europe, Canada, mountainous areas) and why.
lessons.independent_task: Children mark snowy regions on a world map, recording reasoning.
key_questions: Where does it snow in winter?
Why does it snow there?

differentiation.greater_depth: Mark 5+ regions and explain reasoning using latitude/altitude simply

lessons.assessment_notes: Note locational knowledge of weather patterns — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about whether snow is common where you live.

lessons.title: Ice: Solid to Liquid
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to observe and describe ice melting into water.
success_criteria: I can describe ice melting.
I can say this is a change of state.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap ice melting from Year 1 Week 20.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model observing ice melting, introducing the terms solid and liquid for this change.
lessons.independent_task: Children observe ice melting and record their observations using the terms solid/liquid.
key_questions: What is happening to the ice?
What do we call the ice and the water?

differentiation.support: Observe with adult support, simple recording
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the change of state using correct vocabulary

lessons.assessment_notes: Note introduction of solid/liquid vocabulary for material changes — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Recap solid and liquid states discussed.
lessons.home_link: Watch ice melt at home and describe what happens.

lessons.title: Writing About Winter in Another Country
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write descriptive sentences about winter weather elsewhere.
success_criteria: I can describe winter somewhere else.
I can use an expanded noun phrase.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap facts about world winter weather from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a descriptive sentence about winter in another country using an expanded noun phrase.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences describing winter in a chosen country.
key_questions: What is winter like there?
Can you use an expanded noun phrase?

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 4+ sentences with varied noun phrases

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive writing and grammar application — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share winter descriptions with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Describe winter in a country to your family.

lessons.title: Quarter Hour Time: Winter Schedules
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply quarter hour time-telling to a winter-themed schedule.
success_criteria: I can read quarter hour times.
I can answer a question about a schedule.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap quarter hour times from Week 8.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a winter-activity-themed schedule using quarter hour times.
lessons.independent_task: Children read and answer questions about a quarter-hour schedule.
key_questions: What time does this activity start?
How long until the next one?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note consolidation of quarter hour time-telling — evidence for MATHS.MEA.

lessons.title: Winter Clothing Around the World
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how winter clothing varies around the world.
success_criteria: I can describe winter clothing in a cold place.
I can compare it to clothing in a milder place.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how winter clothing varies by climate severity around the world.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare winter clothing needs in two different countries, recording differences.
key_questions: What would you wear here in winter?
How is this different from another place?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of climate knowledge to clothing — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about your winter clothing at home.

lessons.title: Freezing: Liquid to Solid
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to observe and describe water freezing into ice.
success_criteria: I can describe water freezing.
I can say this reverses the melting.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss freezing as the reverse of melting, predicting what will happen to water left in a freezer.
lessons.independent_task: Children predict and (over time) observe water freezing, recording their observations.
resources_needed: access to a freezer if possible, or discuss/observe pre-frozen samples
key_questions: What do you think will happen to the water?
Is freezing the opposite of melting?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the reversible nature of the change in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of reversible material changes — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Recap freezing and melting as reversible changes.
lessons.home_link: Predict what happens to water in a freezer at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Winter Weather Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read winter-weather-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read winter weather words.
I can read a sentence about winter.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to winter-weather-themed words (e.g. 'freeze', 'blizzard', 'chilly').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
key_questions: Can you read this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading winter weather words over the week.

lessons.title: Winter Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a winter context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a winter context (e.g. snowballs made/thrown).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve winter-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
key_questions: How many altogether?
How many are left?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a winter word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Winter Activities Around the World
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe winter activities enjoyed in different places.
success_criteria: I can name a winter activity.
I can say where it might happen.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss winter activities around the world (skiing, ice skating, Diwali/Christmas lights, warm-country winter beach visits).
lessons.independent_task: Children match winter activities to likely locations, recording reasoning.
resources_needed: Winter activity and location picture cards
key_questions: Where might this activity happen?
Why?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of climate/culture knowledge to activities — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a winter activity your family enjoys.

lessons.title: Winter Weather Reporter
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present a short weather report clearly.
success_criteria: I can describe the weather.
I can present it clearly to the class.
lessons.starter_activity: Watch/discuss a short example of a weather report.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model presenting a simple weather report for a chosen country's winter weather.
lessons.independent_task: Children present a short weather report for a chosen country to a small group.
key_questions: What is the weather like there?
Can you present it clearly?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and presentation skill applied to a geography context — evidence for ENG.SL1/GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Present a weather report to your family.

lessons.title: Symmetry in Snowflakes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a symmetrical snowflake pattern.
success_criteria: I can create a symmetrical pattern.
I can explain how it's symmetrical.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating a symmetrical snowflake using the fold-and-cut technique.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own symmetrical snowflake pattern.
key_questions: Is your snowflake symmetrical?
How do you know?

differentiation.greater_depth: Create a more complex symmetrical design

lessons.assessment_notes: Note symmetry consolidation — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Make a symmetrical snowflake or pattern at home.

lessons.title: Winter World Map Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to synthesise the week's learning onto a class world map.
success_criteria: I can add a country to the class map.
I can add one winter fact about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all countries studied this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss contributing to a large class world map display.
lessons.independent_task: Children add their researched country and winter fact to a large class world map.
key_questions: Where does your country go?
What winter fact will you add?

differentiation.greater_depth: Add detailed facts and help others place their countries

lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's locational knowledge — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.plenary: Admire the completed class world map.
lessons.home_link: Describe the class winter world map to your family.

lessons.title: Winter Weather Around the World Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about world winter weather.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's winter weather learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about world winter weather, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Where is it coldest in winter?
Why might people dress differently in winter around the world?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on world winter weather facts.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Temperature, Time, Symmetry
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply temperature, time, and symmetry skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can compare temperatures.
I can tell quarter hour times.
I can identify symmetry.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of temperature comparison, quarter hour time-telling, and symmetry.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
key_questions: Which is colder?
What time is this?
Is this symmetrical?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 20 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA/GEO.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising telling the time over the weekend.

lessons.title: Winter Weather and Materials Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about winter weather and material states.
success_criteria: I can name a feature of winter weather somewhere.
I can describe melting and freezing.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's science and geography vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering world winter weather, melting, and freezing.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Winter Weather Around the World' display, completing Spring 1.
key_questions: What have we learned about winter weather and materials?
What was most interesting?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: End of Spring 1 half-term consolidation summary — evidence for SCI.MAT/GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate a great Spring 1 half-term of learning.
lessons.home_link: Share your favourite thing you learned this half-term with your family.
